invariants: Dependencies point inward only: Domain <- Application <- Adapters <- Delivery, and no inner layer names an outer one.
Surface is Delivery and therefore outer; it is never an inner layer and never a layer of its own.
AI agent and infrastructure concerns are outer adapters, never Domain or Application.
The Onion applies to code-bearing backend and archetype work only; planning, prompt and governance material is not placed in a layer.

axisInvariants: The WBS metaphor, the seven lifecycle phases, prompts, multi-agent, evidence, governance and the Control/Data/AI planes are separate meta-framework axes.
No axis is an Onion layer and no Onion layer is an axis; mapping one onto the other is a category error and fails closed.
An axis may cut across every Onion layer without changing the inward dependency direction.

sequence.scope: One PostgreSQL substrate: schema baseline, row-level security policies per tenant, explicit transaction boundaries, a transactional outbox table with a relay contract, and an append-only audit trail.
nonGoals: no kernel primitive
no typed action or PDP
no SDK generation
no app, module or surface
no release, deploy or production path
sequence.red: Failing migration, RLS-isolation, transaction-atomicity, outbox-delivery and audit-append tests exist and fail before any schema or policy is written.
sequence.green: Those tests pass against a real PostgreSQL instance with RLS forced, transactions atomic, outbox rows written in the same transaction as their source change, and audit rows append-only.
sequence.rollback: Revert the migration, the RLS policies, the outbox and audit objects and their tests as one shard; no dependent code exists yet.
exitCriteria: npm test and npm run check pass
no primitive, SDK, app or surface file is touched

sequence.scope: Kernel primitives with typed action and envelope contracts and a policy decision point, built on the substrate from step 1.
nonGoals: no SDK generation
no app, module or surface
no schema redesign
no release, deploy or production path
sequence.red: Failing contract tests for primitive boundaries, typed action and envelope shape, and PDP allow/deny decisions exist first.
sequence.green: Primitives expose typed actions through validated envelopes and every action is authorised by the PDP against the RLS-backed substrate.
sequence.rollback: Revert the primitives, the typed action and envelope contracts, the PDP and their tests as one shard; the substrate stays untouched.
exitCriteria: no adapter or delivery concern leaks inward
npm test and npm run check pass

sequence.scope: One generated SDK derived from the typed action and envelope contracts of step 2, with a pinned public boundary.
nonGoals: no hand-written client surface
no app or module
no contract change smuggled through generation
no release, deploy or production path
sequence.red: Failing generation-determinism, public-boundary and contract-parity tests exist first.
sequence.green: The SDK regenerates byte-identically from the pinned contracts, exposes only the declared public boundary and stays in parity with the primitives.
sequence.rollback: Revert the generator, the generated SDK and their tests as one shard; primitives and substrate stay untouched.
exitCriteria: npm test and npm run check pass

sequence.scope: Exactly one end-to-end golden slice through Delivery -> Adapters -> Application -> Domain and back, using the SDK from step 3 against the substrate from step 1.
nonGoals: no second slice
no product build-out
no release, deploy or production path
no GO-PRODUCTION claim
sequence.red: A failing end-to-end test for the single slice exists first, covering authorisation, transaction, outbox and audit evidence.
sequence.green: The one slice passes end to end with tenant isolation held, the transaction atomic, an outbox row emitted and an audit row appended.
sequence.rollback: Revert the slice and its test as one shard; SDK, primitives and substrate stay untouched.
exitCriteria: the single slice is GREEN end to end
npm test and npm run check pass
